claims.statement: Mintlify is the static site generator responsible for rendering the built documentation from /build/ into docs.langchain.com. The LangChain documentation pipeline produces markdown and MDX output in /build/, and Mintlify reads this output along with site configuration from docs.json to render the final site.

Site configuration is defined in /src/docs.json (copied to /build/docs.json) using Mintlify's docs.json schema, specifying navigation menus, theme (aspen), fonts (TWK Lausanne for headings, Inter for body), icons (Tabler library), colors, analytics (Google Tag Manager), contextual actions, and URL redirects.

The development workflow uses mint dev CLI (a separate global npm binary installed via npm install -g mint@latest) running in the /build/ directory on port 3000. The docs dev command in pipeline/commands/dev.py orchestrates file watching via FileWatcher and launches mint dev as an async subprocess.

Mintlify is configured with three OpenAPI sections: committed Agent Server and LangSmith REST specifications generate under langsmith/agent-server-api and langsmith/smith-api, while the Control Plane specification is fetched from https://api.host.langchain.com/openapi.json at deployment. The LangSmith REST specification is refreshed daily through a standing update PR workflow.

The Mint link-check targets build first, run from build/ with redirect checking, filter deployment-time OpenAPI routes, standalone-snippet sections, and documented checker false positives, and fail only for remaining actionable indented link entries. The reusable link-check workflow uses Node 22 and runs the anchor check plus the Agent Server OpenAPI validation.

The preview workflow builds artifacts for same-repository pull requests, pushes them to a preview branch, and invokes Mintlify's preview API only after validating the required API key, project ID, and branch name. On closed pull requests, cleanup recomputes the deterministic branch, also sweeps legacy preview names based on a source-branch prefix, and refuses to delete a branch without the `preview-` prefix.
Mintlify deployment generates endpoint routes for the configured OpenAPI sections, so those routes are absent from local build output and are intentionally filtered from local Mint link checking.

Managed Deep Agents source pages are emitted only at language-prefixed LangSmith routes, while docs.json redirects their unversioned routes to Python; Deep Agents Code is emitted once at an unprefixed OSS route and excluded from OSS language-link rewriting.

The development command performs an initial build unless --skip-build is set, fails if that build fails or if Mint exits nonzero or the watcher stops unexpectedly, and shuts down the watcher and Mint subprocess on interruption.

Preview creation validates source branch syntax and length, derives a deterministic collision-resistant branch name from a sanitized source prefix and hash, keeps the Mintlify preview URL stable across pushes, and updates an existing preview branch with force-with-lease so a concurrent move is rejected rather than silently overwritten.

Mint export rebuilds the documentation and writes build/export.zip by default; it requires a Mint CLI with export support, Node 20 or 22 rather than Node 25 or later, and an Enterprise Mintlify plan. htmltest validates the exported archive with internal paths and hashes disabled because the export is not a complete page set, so it cannot establish internal navigation correctness.
The production publishing workflow builds source on main pushes or manual dispatch, copies build into public/build, and publishes that directory to the prod branch.

Unit tests for the Mint broken-link filter verify that snippet-only sections and known deployment-time or legacy-path exclusions are removed while ordinary broken links remain actionable, and that only the exact SmithDB migration and `n_jobs_per_worker` anchor exclusions apply in anchor mode.

The LangSmith OpenAPI refresh processor accepts only the allow-listed api.smith.langchain.com host, hides fleet, internal, and selected health endpoints from public documentation, assigns and orders human-readable tag groups, and normalizes operation titles including visible non-sandbox v2 labels.

The scheduled LangSmith OpenAPI refresh writes the processed committed specification, exits without a commit when it is unchanged, and otherwise appends to an existing chore/refresh-langsmith-openapi pull request or creates one, ensuring at most one outstanding refresh PR.

Mintlify generates llms.txt and nested /_llms/ indexes only on the deployed site. The weekly coverage job crawls those served indexes from docs.langchain.com and compares their same-site page links with sitemap.xml, failing when any sitemap page is unreachable from llms.txt.
The deployed llms.txt checker uses a dedicated user agent, a 30-second timeout, and up to three attempts for connection-level failures, but lets HTTP errors fail immediately.
`make check-openapi` builds the documentation and runs `mint openapi-check` only on `langsmith/agent-server-openapi.json`; it does not validate the Control Plane or LangSmith REST OpenAPI inputs.

When `--skip-build` is selected, the development command only warns if `build/` is absent and proceeds to start the watcher and Mint process, so the option does not establish that a valid build exists.
Preview creation is skipped for fork pull requests because it needs repository write access, and cleanup refuses to delete a branch without the `preview-` prefix.

The builder creates both Python and JavaScript OSS route trees, but emits a shared OSS page only for the language whose navigation exclusively lists it; shared pages listed in both or neither navigation build for both, while language-specific source files build only for their matching tree.
The builder emits OpenWiki once at the unversioned `oss/openwiki/` route and excludes that route family from OSS language-link rewriting, matching the language-agnostic Deep Agents Code treatment.

Each full documentation build removes any existing `build/` directory before rebuilding Python and JavaScript OSS output, language-agnostic Deep Agents Code and OpenWiki output, LangSmith output, and shared files; `build/` therefore has no durable authoring state.

A pull-request workflow for documentation changes targeting main runs a retired-site check across all authored Markdown and MDX under src/. It rejects links to listed legacy documentation hosts except the Helm repository path, directing docs links to relative routes and API-reference links to reference.langchain.com.

The preview PR comment ranks changed routable Markdown and MDX files by diff size, lists at most five, and constructs candidate deep links by stripping `src/` and extensions, collapsing `index`, and defaulting unprefixed OSS paths to Python. It excludes snippets and code samples but does not consult the builder, navigation, redirects, or generated output, so its source-path mapping is not authoritative for language-selective, unversioned, managed, redirected, or deployment-generated routes.
The reusable documentation-validation workflow pins Mint CLI `4.2.1181`, uses Node 22, and runs the anchor-aware link check, MDX validation, and Agent Server OpenAPI validation.
